answer: The challenge noted regarding holding private actors responsible for AI existential risks under international human rights law is that private actors are currently under no legal obligation to take precautions to address AI as an existential threat. International human rights law traditionally places obligations solely on state actors, reflecting a vertical relationship between the citizen and the state. While there is some movement toward recognizing that private actors may be subjected to human rights obligations, this has not yet emerged as a matter of international law, leaving it up to corporations to decide the extent to which they wish to incorporate human rights compliance in their practices.
